# General Review Lessons

- Make a guard's zero-match check count only the matches it is meant to protect. Matches that are always present, like the guard's own allowed cases, keep the check from ever firing.
- Test a guard by planting a violation and by breaking its detection, and see it fail both times. A guard that passes on clean code proves nothing.
- Before acting on a review finding, check whether existing tests or contracts explain the current shape. A structural test can be why the code looks the way it does.
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model. Any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path. Otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
- Before setting an explicit timeout, look up the platform's current default for that exact event; an explicit value can shorten the budget rather than add one.
- When splitting known from unknown JSON keys to preserve them, decode only the exact known keys and keep every other key, case variants included, as unknown. `encoding/json` matches field names case-insensitively, so decoding the whole object lets a key like `"Command"` overwrite the real field.
- When a change makes a fix command riskier, changes which command to run, or adds a new place that reports an existing failure, check every place that already reports it (status, doctor, enable, help text) so they all give the same fix. Otherwise one screen sends people to the safe fix and the next to the destructive one, or one command prints the same failure twice with different fixes.
- When a test plants a failure to cover an error branch, make sure an earlier step doesn't fail first; otherwise the assertion passes without ever running that branch.
- Select an agent's final report by a marker it carries (such as the contract line), not by its position in the event stream; a trailing tool call or an empty message ID moves a position-based boundary.
- When code keeps state so a later run can retry, test the retry itself. A test that checks the kept state against the same expression the code uses would pass even if that expression were wrong.
- When decoding user-editable JSON into maps or pointers, skip null elements before writing to them; `[null]` decodes to a nil map and a write panics.
- Review a PR that is behind main against current main, not its own base: build both and run the same repro. Its tests pass on its old base even when keeping its side of a conflict would undo a fix merged since.
- When wiring user config into a new path, test it with a broken config too. A user rule that silently fails to load leaks the same way as one that was never wired.
- Make a fail-closed check fire only on the failure it guards against, not on a whole class of errors. A refusal on any settings error blocks unrelated cases and pushes users toward a less safe escape hatch, such as an unredacted `--raw` bundle.
- Read the Trail's current description and resolved findings before drafting review comments. The trail description can be newer than the PR description and may already list known follow-ups, which turns "you missed this" into a question about scale or timing.
- When a PR claims corpus validation, check what the corpus contained, and test on inputs from outside it, such as other languages and other codebases. A corpus drawn from one codebase can pass while common idioms elsewhere break.

# Branch review: `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`

**Verdict: request changes**

Scope: `main...fix-checkpoint-trailer-block` at `2d16b3666`, covering one commit and seven changed files.

## Author intent

The change separates two meanings that the old checkpoint parser conflated:

- Whole-message parsing remains available for historical discovery, especially GitHub and native Git squash commits containing several embedded checkpoint trailers.
- Final-trailer-block parsing authorizes checkpoint creation, reuse, and mutation.

That split is the right design. The hook and attach changes apply it in several important places without breaking the existing squash-resume tests. The implementation is not complete, however: two mutation paths still trust whole-message results, and the strict parser does not match Git's trailer grammar.

No pull request currently exists for this branch. The related [PR #2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168) remains open.

## Spec

### Act on

#### High: `checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` can write to a body-selected checkpoint

[`runExplainAuto`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L617) and [`runExplainCommit`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L2994) still resolve commit linkage with whole-message `ParseCheckpoint`. When `--generate` is present, that ID reaches [`store.Write`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L1095).

A commit body can therefore name an existing but unrelated checkpoint and cause:

```text
commit body
    -> ParseCheckpoint(existing ID)
    -> checkpoint explain --generate --force
    -> generateCheckpointSummary
    -> store.Write(existing ID)
```

This violates the recorded requirement to "prevent untrusted checkpoint-shaped commit-body text from being accepted in unsafe contexts."

Use final-block parsing when commit resolution leads to summary generation. Keep whole-message parsing only for read-only discovery. Add regressions for both explicit `--commit` and positional commit fallback.

#### Medium: legacy migration still lets body text authorize reconciliation

[`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go#L72) scans the whole message when a legacy state lacks `LastCheckpointCommitHash`. A matching body ID advances both `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit`, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution.

This conflicts with the intended boundary that body IDs are discovery candidates while final-block IDs authorize mutation.

Require final-block evidence for the legacy fallback, or decline reconciliation when the recorded commit hash is unavailable. Add a legacy-state regression with a matching body ID followed by a different final trailer block.

### Consider

None.

### Noted

The existing squash-history semantics are preserved. All three named squash-resume unit tests passed unchanged.

### Dismissed

None.

**Worst spec issue:** `--generate` can persist a summary to a checkpoint selected solely by commit-body text.

## Standards

### Act on

#### High: leading whitespace turns body text into an authorizing trailer

[`ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L162) and [`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L306) left-trim lines before classifying and parsing them.

This line is therefore accepted:

```text
  Entire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6
```

Git 2.50's `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns no trailer for the same message. The branch parser nevertheless lets that line choose the ID used by PostCommit condensation and attach.

Do not remove leading spaces or tabs when validating final-block trailer lines. Add production-path regressions for PostCommit and attach, not only parser tests.

#### Medium: commit-message comment handling does not follow Git configuration

[`parseCheckpointFromCommitMessageFile`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L290) strips only `#` suffix lines. Git permits a configurable `core.commentChar`, and default cleanup preserves comment-prefixed lines when no editor runs. See the official [`git commit` cleanup documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit/2.52.0).

This creates two failure shapes:

- A repository using another comment character can hide a legitimate final trailer behind Git's comment block.
- A `git commit -m` or `-F` message can contain real `#` user content that this helper discards before deciding an earlier checkpoint-shaped body line is final.

Resolve Git's effective comment character or apply Git-equivalent cleanup rules. Cover editor, `-m`/`-F`, and custom-comment-character flows.

### Consider

#### Support Git trailer continuations

[`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L317) walks backward only while every line independently matches `Key: value`. Git accepts continuation lines beginning with whitespace, so a multiline trailer after `Entire-Checkpoint` can make the branch parser reject the entire block even though Git accepts it.

This may produce a duplicate checkpoint ID during prepare/amend or make PostCommit skip condensation. Either support continuation lines or explicitly document and test the narrower grammar.

#### Exercise attach through its durable boundary

`TestAttachIgnoresCheckpointShapedBodyText` calls `resolveCheckpointID` and `promptAmendCommit` separately. It does not prove through `runAttach` that a forged checkpoint remains unmodified and a fresh checkpoint receives the attached session.

A full-path regression should inspect the persistent store after attach.

### Noted

- The strict maintainability pass found no structural regression. The large hook file was already over 1,000 lines; this change did not cross that threshold or scatter the core parser policy.
- The parser change adds no lock or interruption point. Parser selection occurs before existing writes, so cleanup and recovery semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- Median `PrepareCommitMsg` time was 15.20 ms on this branch versus 15.13 ms on `main`, a difference of roughly 0.5% and within sample noise.

### Dismissed

One adversarial reviewer flagged `hasUserContent` for treating every checkpoint-shaped line as Entire metadata. That behavior predates this branch and requires a commit whose only user content is itself checkpoint-shaped. It is not a regression introduced here.

**Worst standards issue:** the strict parser accepts a Git-invalid indented body line as mutation authority.

## Correctness model

### Who owns each write?

- PrepareCommitMsg chooses the checkpoint ID; PostCommit owns condensation into persistent checkpoint storage.
- Attach chooses or reuses an ID, writes the attached session, then best-effort amends the commit.
- `checkpoint explain --generate` owns summary persistence.
- Session migration owns `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` reconciliation.

The first two owners now use the strict parser in their main paths. Summary generation and legacy migration do not.

### What happens around interruption?

The diff changes classification before existing writes. It does not add a lock, subprocess, temporary file, or new partial-write state. Existing write and recovery owners remain responsible before and after the decision. The outstanding risk is wrong-target mutation, not new interruption behavior.

### Which tests observe the real contract?

- The PrepareCommitMsg regression enters the production hook and would fail on the old code.
- The attach test observes helpers rather than the durable store contract.
- No regression covers body-selected summary generation, legacy migration, indented pseudo-trailers, custom Git comment characters, or trailer continuation lines.

## Multi-model agreement

Three independent reviewers examined the same intent and diff:

| Finding | Agreement | Disposition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Explain generation trusts body IDs | 3/3 | Act on |
| Indented pseudo-trailer accepted | 2/3 | Act on |
| Legacy migration trusts body IDs | 2/3 | Act on |
| Git comment handling is hard-coded | 1/3 | Act on after local verification |
| `hasUserContent` removes body-shaped lines | 1/3 | Dismissed as pre-existing |

## Verification performed

- Focused trailer parser tests passed.
- Focused PrepareCommitMsg and attach tests passed.
- `TestFindCheckpointInHistory_MultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestFindBranchCheckpoint_SquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestResumeFromCurrentBranch_MultipleCheckpointsSaysLatest` passed.
- `git diff --check main..HEAD` passed.
- Git 2.50 rejected indented pseudo-trailers and accepted continuation-line trailer blocks in direct `git interpret-trailers --parse` checks.
- Checkpoint history records a successful pre-commit `mise run check`; the full gate was not rerun during this read-only review.

## Recommendation

Request changes. Close the two remaining mutation paths first, then make the strict parser agree with Git about indentation and comment cleanup. Preserve whole-message discovery for squash history throughout.

AUTHOR: MuskanPaliwal
LABELS: 
## Summary

Checkpoint resolution parses trailers out of the whole commit message, including in code paths that decide whether to create, reuse, or mutate checkpoint storage. A line shaped like `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` anywhere in the body is indistinguishable from a real squashed trailer. So a commit body that names an existing checkpoint ID, whether pasted, reverted, or written by someone else, gets treated as authority over that checkpoint.

## Impact

A commit body naming an existing checkpoint ID can:

- make PostCommit condensation bind the commit to a checkpoint that has nothing to do with it, instead of minting a fresh one
- make `entire checkpoint attach` write the attached session into the unrelated checkpoint
- make `entire checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` persist a generated summary into it via `store.Write`
- make legacy session migration (`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`) advance `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` off a body ID, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution

Checking that the ID exists in storage doesn't help. Existence proves nothing about the ID's relationship to this commit.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Work in a repo with Entire enabled, in an agent session that has already produced at least one checkpoint. Note an existing checkpoint ID from `entire checkpoint list` (call it `<unrelated-id>`).
2. Make an unrelated code change in a new agent session.
3. Commit it with a message whose body contains a checkpoint-shaped line naming the existing ID:

   ```sh
   git commit -m "innocent change

   Entire-Checkpoint: <unrelated-id>"
   ```

4. Let the PostCommit hook run, then inspect `entire checkpoint list` and the commit's linkage.

**Expected:** the body line is ignored. The commit gets a fresh checkpoint for the new session's work.

**Actual:** the parser picks up `<unrelated-id>` from the body and condensation binds the commit to that unrelated checkpoint. The same forged line steers `attach`, `explain --generate`, and legacy migration, since they resolve IDs through the same whole-message parse.

The indented variant also works, even though Git itself doesn't consider it a trailer: `  Entire-Checkpoint: <unrelated-id>` (leading whitespace) is left-trimmed before classification and accepted, while `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns nothing for the same message.

## Root cause

One parser answers two different questions.

Discovery asks which checkpoints a commit's history mentions. Scanning the whole message is correct there, because GitHub and native squash commits embed several checkpoint trailers in the body.

Authorization asks which checkpoint an operation may mutate. Only the final trailer block can answer that, and the parser never made the distinction.

The parser is also looser than Git's own trailer grammar, which widens the hole. Besides the indentation issue above, commit-message-file cleanup hard-codes `#` instead of honoring `core.commentChar`.

## Suggested fix

Split the parser in two. Keep whole-message parsing for read-only discovery only (squash-history resume, listing), so commits with several embedded trailers keep working. Add a strict parser that reads only the final trailer block and matches Git's grammar: no leading whitespace, comment-char-aware cleanup. Route every mutation decision through the strict parser: commit hooks, attach, `explain --generate`, and legacy migration reconciliation. When the recorded commit hash is unavailable in migration, decline reconciliation rather than trusting body text.

Related: #2168 covers broader trailer-line anchoring and doesn't overlap with this.

`AppendCheckpointTrailer` could write a trailer that neither `git interpret-trailers --parse` nor our own strict readers accept. `entire checkpoint attach` then printed a successful amend for linkage that did not exist.

## The mismatch

The writer and the readers disagreed about one character, leading whitespace.

`finalTrailerBlock` classifies raw lines on purpose. Git treats an indented line after a trailer as a continuation of that trailer's value, never as a new trailer. `appendTrailerLine` ran `strings.TrimSpace` before calling `IsTrailerLine`, so an indented `  Foo: bar` looked like a trailer to the writer and like body text to every reader.

A message whose final paragraph is an indented pseudo-trailer got the new trailer joined onto that paragraph with no blank line above it. The result is one paragraph that is not a trailer block, and three things follow from it:

- `attach` reported `Amended commit ... with Entire-Checkpoint: B`.
- `PostCommit` re-read the commit, found no trailer, and skipped linkage.
- `attach`'s own dedup check could not see the trailer either, so a second run appended another copy.

The commit ends up carrying trailer text that no consumer recognises, and the user is told the opposite.

## The fix

I pulled `finalTrailerBlock`'s classification loop into a shared `isTrailerBlock(lines []string) bool`, and the writer now classifies the final non-comment paragraph with it, on raw lines. One grammar, two callers. A paragraph the writer will join has to be one the readers accept.

Joining also requires a blank line between that paragraph and the content above it. That guard keeps a trailer-shaped subject line such as `fix: bug`, which `IsTrailerLine` matches for good reason, from having the trailer glued onto it. Sharing the grammar without the guard would fix the indented case and break the far more common one.

`finalTrailerBlock` behaves exactly as before. `isTrailerBlock` returns false for an empty slice, which covers the old `start == end` guard, and the old loop could only reach its final return with `seenTrailer` already true, since a non-trailer first line always hit the `default` arm.

## Scope

Whole-message occurrences stay discovery candidates, so squash resume keeps working. Only final-block placement authorizes mutation, which is the boundary #2253 sets. `ParseCheckpoint` and `ParseAllCheckpoints` are untouched.

I proved the red state by restoring the pre-fix `trailers.go` under the new tests. Five subtests fail, and all five pass with the fix:

I confirmed two bugs with real git in the new comment-character handling. Main has also added its own checkpoint-provenance model since this branch was last updated, so the PR needs re-scoping against main, not a mechanical rebase. My notes for the #2259 session are in the shared folder (`pr-2253-review.md`).

## 1. Worktree vs published PR

- Local HEAD `7be8499d4` is the PR head and matches `origin/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`. There are no tracked changes.
- Two untracked files, both your local notes from Sep 2 and not part of the PR:
  - **`progress.md`** (17 lines): a session log for the original change, with tech notes and the test gates it claims passed.
  - **`review.md`** (163 lines): a self-review of the first commit `2d16b3666`, before the PR existed, with a "request changes" verdict. Its six points (explain `--generate`, legacy migration, indented trailers, comment character, continuation lines, a full-path attach test) all have a fix and a test in later PR commits.
- I left both files untouched.

## 2. Brief

**What it does for users.** Entire stops trusting `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` text in the body of a commit message when deciding which checkpoint to create, reuse or write to. Only the commit's final trailer block (the last paragraph, laid out the way git lays out trailers) counts.

**Why.** Today a pasted or reverted body line naming an existing checkpoint can steer PostCommit condensation, `attach`, `explain --generate` and legacy migration into an unrelated checkpoint (#2255).

**How.**
- It adds strict final-block parsers to `trailers.go`. They accept no leading whitespace and allow indented continuation lines.
- It switches the code paths that write checkpoints to the strict parsers. Whole-message parsing stays for read-only discovery, so squash history keeps working.
- It makes commit-message cleanup honor `core.commentChar` / `core.commentString` / `auto`.

**Performance.** It adds 1 to 2 `git config` subprocesses per editor-flow commit. This hasn't been measured.

**Compatibility.** Body trailers no longer link commits for writes. Squash commits change behavior in `attach` and `explain --generate`.

**Data.** There is no format change.

**Risk.** Mostly wrong-target versus missed-link tradeoffs.

**Uncertain.** How much of #2255 still reproduces on current main.

## 3. Findings (most severe first)

1. **High: the PR is stale against a redesign on main.**
   - The dry-run merge conflicts in `attach.go`, `explain.go`, `manual_commit_hooks.go` and `trailers.go`. `manual_commit_migration.go` and its test were deleted on main (`b126c2e8f`, shadow-branch removal), so that hunk, its test and the issue's fourth impact bullet no longer apply.
   - Main now has a provenance model (Peyton Montei, Sep 18 to 24): `stampedTrailer`, `stampedTrailersOf` and `stampedByAnotherCommit` in `manual_commit_provenance.go`, squash-trailer inheritance, a scissors-aware `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, and an adversarial integration suite.
   - PostCommit on main already refuses "to condense into a checkpoint this session did not stamp" when the checkpoint exists locally. The PR's main claim may already be fixed there.
   - Likely still open on main:
     - Prepare's whole-message `stampedTrailer` lets a body ID suppress the fresh trailer.
     - A body ID that isn't in the local store gets condensed under that ID.
     - Attach still parses the whole message in `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`.
   - This lesson applies: "Review a PR behind main against current main."

2. **High (confirmed): `core.commentChar=auto` breaks editor commits.**
   - `gitCommentPrefix` ([manual_commit_hooks.go:323](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:323)) guesses the character from a file where git has already written its comment block. So it always rules out git's real choice and picks the next character.
   - I ran real git 2.50 with the PR's functions as the hook. Git used `#`, the PR picked `;`, and this was committed:
     ```
     Entire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6
     ; Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link this commit to Claude Code session context.
     ```
   - `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns nothing for that message, and the PR's own final-block PostCommit check ([:1001](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:1001)) would skip condensation. The base branch handled this case correctly.
   - `TestGitCommentPrefixAutoAvoidsExistingLinePrefix` ([manual_commit_test.go:1023](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go:1023)) passes only because it feeds in a message without git's comment block.

3. **Medium: #2253 alone breaks linking for some `-m` messages.** `appendTrailerLine` ([trailers.go:243](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:243)) still trims whitespace before checking a line. So it appends onto an indented `  Key: value` paragraph that the new `finalTrailerBlock` ([:307](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:307)) rejects. #2259 is exactly this fix.

4. **Medium: the `explain --generate` hunk adds no protection and creates an inconsistency.**
   - `generateCheckpointSummary` summarizes a checkpoint's own transcript into that same checkpoint, and `explain --checkpoint <id> --generate` already accepts any ID.
   - Meanwhile `parseCheckpointForExplainCommit` ([explain.go:3025](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:3025)) uses different IDs per mode. On a GitHub squash commit, the read-only view shows checkpoint A, while `--generate` summarizes B or fails with "has no Entire-Checkpoint trailer".
   - One option is to drop this hunk, per the lesson "make a fail-closed check fire only on the failure it guards against."

5. **Medium: `attach` on a squash-merge HEAD changes behavior.** [attach.go:653](cmd/entire/cli/attach.go:653) now creates a fresh ID and prompts to amend, where it used to join the existing checkpoint. Main rewrote attach to join or rewrite and to never rewrite pushed commits, so this needs a decision there.

6. **Low (confirmed): the precedence between the two settings is wrong** ([:324](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:324)). Git treats `core.commentString` and `core.commentChar` as aliases where the last one set wins. With commentString set first and commentChar second, the PR's `//` helper lines got committed. The test at [manual_commit_test.go:1016](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go:1016) asserts the wrong rule. A single `git config --get-regexp` call that takes the last value would fix it and halve the subprocesses.

7. **Low:** the hook cost hasn't been measured. The 0.5% figure in `review.md` predates the subprocesses.

8. **Low (confirmed):** with `commit -v` or `commit.verbose`, stripping comment lines leaves the diff as the final paragraph. That makes an existing trailer invisible during amend. Main already has scissors handling the PR could reuse.

9. **Low:** the parser is stricter than git, though the PR body says it "follows Git trailer structure":
   - `Entire-Checkpoint:abc` with no space is rejected, and so is a block containing a `(cherry picked from ...)` line.
   - A continuation line is accepted, although git reads the whole value as `a1b2c3d4e5f6 continuation text`.
   - `hasUserContent` still hard-codes `#`.

**Lessons check:**
- General.md: the behind-main lesson (finding 1) and the fail-closed lesson (finding 4) apply.
- cli.md's lesson about replacing a git subprocess with a parser doesn't apply here.

I'd propose one new General.md lesson, pending your approval: "When a hook copies a git decision, run real git and look at the file the hook receives. Git may already have applied that decision (the auto comment character, scissors, sign-off) before the hook runs."

#2259 says "merge #2253 first", and finding 3 shows #2253 shouldn't ship without it. But #2259's head `ef07a954a` doesn't contain #2253's last two commits (`931e3a746`, `7be8499d4`, which also edits `trailers.go`). 1. Rerun the #2255 repro in a temp repo against current main, to see what still reproduces.
2. Draft a short question for the maintainers on whether final-block authority fits main's provenance model. I'd show you the text first.

Fixes #2256

An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere in a commit message still decides which checkpoint a commit writes to. Main's provenance check (`stampedByAnotherCommit`) only refuses a checkpoint that already exists in the local store, so a checkpoint ID in a commit body, whether pasted, quoted, indented, or mentioned mid-sentence, still steers three writes.

This PR now also carries #2259 (the trailer writer fix). The stricter reader here is what makes that writer bug reachable, so the two need to land together, and I'm closing #2259 in favour of this one.

## Problem

I ported the scenarios onto current main and ran them there:

| Scenario on main | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `entire attach` on a commit whose body says `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` | The attached session is written into `<id>`, which ends up holding two unrelated sessions. Same for an indented line and for "Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: <id> from last week." |
| `git commit -m` with that line in the body, `<id>` not in this clone | prepare-commit-msg treats it as already stamped and adds no trailer. Post-commit then condenses the session's work under `<id>`, claiming an ID that may belong to a teammate's unfetched checkpoint. |
| Same, `<id>` already in this clone | Post-commit correctly refuses to write there, but the commit ends up with no checkpoint at all. |
| `entire explain --commit <sha> --generate` | Resolves the first mention anywhere in the message. |

## Cause

Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers with `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints`, whose regex is unanchored and scans the whole message. That is right for discovery, since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrong for deciding a write.

## Fix

Only the final trailer block, read by git's grammar, decides a write:

- `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (post-commit)
- the amend handler, which still treats a deleted ID mentioned anywhere as stripped, as main does
- attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, switched together so joining and resolving agree
- explain's `--generate` paths; read-only explain keeps whole-message discovery

Prepare reads the message as git will record it: an editor message loses its `#` lines and everything from a scissors line down (`trailers.StripEditorComments`), while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps `#` lines as content, the same rule `addInheritedCheckpointTrailer` already follows. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, and never reads the subject paragraph as trailers. The writer from #2259 uses the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.

Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution, read-only explain), squash and redo inheritance, and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.

## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

I merged current main into this branch first, so the call sites below were main's code when these failed:

- `integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` drives the real prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hook binaries. `TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint`, `TestTrailerAuthority_IndentedLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint`, `TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingExistingCheckpoint` and `TestTrailerAuthority_AgentCommitWithBodyLine` failed with `prepare-commit-msg must stamp a trailer in the final block`. `TestTrailerAuthority_VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` is a guard: it passes before and after, and fails if the editor-message cleanup is skipped.
- `TestAttach_BodyCheckpointLineDoesNotSelectCheckpoint`, `TestAttach_IndentedCheckpointLineDoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestAttach_CheckpointMentionedInProseDoesNotSelectCheckpoint` failed with `attach wrote the session into checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6, which the commit only mentions in its body`.
- `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer` failed with `references checkpoint deadbeefcafe via its Entire-Checkpoint trailer: checkpoint not found`. `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` guards discovery.
- The subject-paragraph cases in `trailers_test.go` failed before that rule was added.

I also ran a throwaway property check over random messages built from a fixed set of lines (plain, indented, continuation, `#`, CRLF, trailer-shaped subjects). In 20,000 messages the writer's output was always read back by the final-block reader, all 500 sampled outputs parsed in `git interpret-trailers --parse`, and in 1,500 messages the reader never accepted a checkpoint that git rejects. It was stricter than git in 36, which is the safe direction.

## Rejected alternatives

- Anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts: a body line could still steer writes, and indented squash messages would stop being discovered.
- Checking only that the named checkpoint exists: existence says nothing about whether this commit stamped it, and it misses IDs this clone has not fetched.
- Keeping this PR's earlier `core.commentChar` detection: its `auto` mode picks the wrong character once git has written its comment block. Main hard-codes `#` today, so comment-character support belongs in a separate change.

## Known gap

`git commit -m … -e` reports source `message` while git still strips comments, so a `-m` message whose own trailer sits above git's comment block could get a second trailer. It is rare, and matches how main already treats `#` lines for that source.

## Branch history

This branch predates main's provenance model. I merged current main, resolved every call-site conflict to main's version (the legacy migration this PR used to touch is gone), and re-applied the final-block reads to main's call sites in the last commit. The diff against main is the change to review.

content.text:
You're right, my earlier review was of the old head. The #2259 session folded #2259 into #2253 and rebuilt it on main. #2253 is now `9dcb3f66f`, CI is all green, it merges cleanly with today's main, and #2259 is closed. Re-reviewing that head: most of my earlier findings are gone. A Copilot review left 2 open comments, both valid, and I found one new regression in the amend path for users who set `core.commentChar`.

## Worktree

Local HEAD `9dcb3f66f` matches the PR head. The two untracked notes (`progress.md`, `review.md`) are untouched, but both describe the old version of the PR now.

## Brief

**What it does for users.** A checkpoint ID only links a commit when it sits in the commit's final trailer block. An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere else (pasted, indented, or mentioned in prose) can no longer make prepare-commit-msg skip stamping, make post-commit condense under a teammate's unfetched ID, make `attach` write into an unrelated checkpoint, or steer `explain --generate`.

**How.**
- Main's provenance helpers (`stampedTrailer`, `stampedTrailersOf`), the amend handler, attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, and `explain --generate` all read the final block now.
- Prepare first strips `#` lines and anything below a scissors line from editor messages.
- The trailer writer from #2259 shares the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so anything it appends is readable.
- Read-only lookups and squash/redo inheritance still scan the whole message.

**Performance.** No subprocesses are added. The earlier `git config` calls are gone.

**Compatibility.** Some messages git treats as trailers no longer link (findings 2 and 4). Attach on a squash commit whose trailers sit only in the body now creates a fresh checkpoint instead of joining the last squashed one. That's arguably more correct, but it is a behavior change.

**Data and risk.** No format change. The risk is now narrow edge cases where a commit fails to link, not writes into the wrong checkpoint.

## Earlier findings, now resolved

- **Stale against main:** fixed. It merges cleanly with `f36367e6f`, 1 commit behind.
- **#2259 ordering:** folded in.
- **`auto` and precedence bugs:** gone with the comment-character support. It's deferred, and the PR body says why.
- **Hook subprocess cost:** gone.
- **`-v` scissors handling:** fixed, with a guard test.

## Findings

1. **Medium-low, confirmed: amend duplicates the trailer when `core.commentChar` isn't `#`.**
   - `StripEditorComments` ([trailers.go:175](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:175)) only strips `#` lines. With `;`, git's comment block stays as the final paragraph, so [handleAmendCommitMsg](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:805) doesn't see the commit's own trailer and falls through to the restore path.
   - I ran a scratch integration test through `go test -overlay` (nothing written to the repo) against the real hook binary:
     - `#`: the message is unchanged.
     - `;`: the hook appends `Entire-Checkpoint: 8552cd20a890` again, and `git stripspace` with `;` records the trailer twice.
   - Main keeps it, because it parses the whole message there.
   - If the session's `LastCheckpointID` differs from the commit's trailer, the amend would re-link the commit instead of just duplicating.
   - Cheapest fix: read `core.commentChar` once for editor sources and strip that prefix. Don't attempt `auto` detection.

2. **Low, Copilot thread, valid: the separator check is too strict.**
   - `trailerLineRe` ([trailers.go:291](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:291)) requires `": "`.
   - Git accepts `Entire-Checkpoint:<id>` and a tab separator (I checked with `git interpret-trailers`), and so does main's own `checkpointTrailerLineRegex`. With this PR, those forms stop linking.
   - Loosening to `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:` matches git. A URL-only paragraph becomes trailer-shaped, but git treats `https://…` as a trailer too, so that's consistent.

3. **Low, Copilot thread, valid but rare: scissors detection uses substring match.**
   - [trailers.go:179](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:179) cuts at any line containing the marker. Git requires the exact `# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------` line.
   - Main's `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` (:204) has the same pattern.
   - Tightening it to a whole-line match, allowing a trailing `\r`, is cheap.

4. **Low: mixed trailer blocks don't link.**
   - Git accepts a block such as `Entire-Checkpoint: X` / `Signed-off-by: A` / `Refs #123`, because it contains a git-generated trailer and at least 25% trailer lines. `isTrailerBlock` ([trailers.go:380](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:380)) rejects the whole block.
   - So a commit-msg hook that appends a non-trailer line leaves the commit unlinked, where main would have condensed it.
   - Rejecting is the safe direction for deciding writes; the cost is a missed link. A sentence in the PR body would cover it.

5. **Question: is the `explain --generate` hunk worth keeping?** ([explain.go:2794](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:2794))
   - `--generate` summarizes a checkpoint's own transcript, and `explain --checkpoint <id> --generate` already accepts any ID, so the hunk doesn't protect anything.
   - It does let the read-only view and `--generate` pick different checkpoints for the same squash commit.
   - Offered as an option, not a requirement.

## Review lessons

- "Review a PR behind main against current main" is now satisfied.
- The verbose-amend guard test was verified RED, which meets "test a guard by planting a violation."
- I treated both Copilot claims as hypotheses and checked them against git.
- "Make a fail-closed check fire only on the failure it guards against" fits finding 5, as an option.

Proposed lesson for General.md, pending your approval: "When a hook reads a message git prepared, test it with real git output under each setting that shapes that message (comment char, cleanup mode, `-v`). A hard-coded `#` passes every test that writes the message by hand."

## Where it stands

| Item | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Mergeability | `MERGEABLE` / `BLOCKED` (needs an approving review); merges cleanly with main `f36367e6f` |
| CI on `9dcb3f66f` | All green: Tests (core, integration a/b/c, canary git-branch and git-refs, Windows), Lint, CodeQL, License, Binary Size. E2E Control Plane skipped. |
| Reviews | Copilot bot "Changes recommended" with 2 unresolved threads (findings 2 and 3). No human review yet; `cli-maintainers` requested. |
| #2259 | Closed, with a comment pointing here. #2256 is linked via "Fixes". |
| Trail | None. Your notes say a trail created after the PR leaves the project trail empty, so it may not be worth creating now. |

## Recommended next steps

1. Fix findings 1 to 3 in one small commit with regression tests:
   - read the comment character for editor sources;
   - loosen `trailerLineRe`;
   - match the exact scissors line.
2. Reply to the two Copilot threads. I'll show you the text first.
3. Add a line to the PR body on finding 4, and decide on finding 5.

content.text:
Here's the pre-edit brief for fixing findings 1 to 3, plus the two Copilot reply drafts. Nothing is edited yet. While checking, finding 1 turned out wider than I reported: with `;` as the comment character, a fresh editor commit also ends up unlinked, not just amend.

## Problem and evidence

I checked these with scratch tests through `go test -overlay` against the real hook binary. Nothing was written to the repo.

**Finding 1: prepare assumes git's comment character is `#`.**
- **Fresh editor commit, `core.commentChar=;`.** Entire's helper comments are written with `#`, so git keeps them, and they land in the trailer's paragraph:
  ```
  Entire-Checkpoint: bc843f3e1a7d
  # Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link ...
  ```
  The PR's final-block reader returns `[]` for this message, so post-commit doesn't condense it and the commit is unlinked. Main also leaks the helper text, but its whole-message parse still links the commit. So the PR turns a cosmetic bug into a lost link.
- **Amend.** The trailer is hidden behind git's `;` comment block, so the restore path appends it a second time (shown last turn).

**Finding 2: the separator is too strict.**
- The reader returns `[]` for `Entire-Checkpoint:a1b2c3d4e5f6` and for the tab-separated form.
- Git accepts both, and main's own `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` tests treat both as trailers ([trailers_test.go:532](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers_test.go:532)).

**Finding 3: the scissors cut matches a substring.**
- A prose line containing `------------------------ >8 ------------------------` hides the real final trailer below it: the final block is `[a1b2c3d4e5f6]`, but after stripping it's `[]`.
- Git only cuts at the exact line `<comment char> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------`.

## Root cause

- **Finding 1:** three helpers that read or write editor messages hard-code `#`:
  - `StripEditorComments` ([trailers.go:175](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:175)), reached through `preparedFinalTrailers` ([manual_commit_provenance.go:48](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_provenance.go:48)) from `stampedTrailer` and the amend handler at [manual_commit_hooks.go:805](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:805);
  - `addCheckpointTrailerWithComment` ([:2804](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:2804));
  - `addInheritedCheckpointTrailer` ([:2786](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:2786)).
- **Finding 2:** `trailerLineRe` ([trailers.go:291](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:291)) requires `": "`.
- **Finding 3:** `strings.Contains(line, scissorsMarker)` at [trailers.go:179](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:179).

## Proposed change

**1. Resolve git's comment prefix once per editor-source hook run** (`-m`/`-F` skips this entirely) and use it in the three helpers.
- New helper in `strategy`: run `git config --get-regexp '^core\.comment(char|string)$'` and take the last line. The two keys are aliases and the last one set wins; I confirmed git's ordering.
- Unset, or any error, falls back to `#`, which is today's behavior.
- For `auto`, infer the character git chose from the message it handed the hook: the scissors line if there is one, else the first character of the last non-blank line, if it's one of git's candidates `#;@!$%^&|:`. I confirmed git writes its comment block last (with a `#` template, git picked `;` and the last line was `;`).
- `StripEditorComments(message, prefix)` gains a prefix parameter. The three helpers take the prefix.
- Cost: one `git config` subprocess, only on editor sources (human `git commit`, amend, `-c`/`-C`, template, squash). Agent commits use `-m` and pay nothing. I'll measure prepare-commit-msg before and after.

**2. Change `trailerLineRe` to `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:`** (Copilot's suggestion). The reader and writer keep one grammar, and leading whitespace is still rejected.

**3. Make `StripEditorComments` cut only at the exact line `<prefix> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------`**, allowing a trailing `\r`.

## Decisions for you

1. **Where to loosen the separator (finding 2).**
   - **Shared grammar (my pick):** a one-line change that matches git exactly. Side effect: the writer now joins onto a final paragraph like a bare `https://…` line instead of starting a new paragraph. Git treats that line as a trailer too (`https: //example.com/x`).
   - **Reader only:** no formatting change, and still safe, because everything the writer joins is something the reader accepts. But it breaks the "one grammar" contract #2259 set up.
2. **Whether to include `auto` inference.** I recommend yes, since markdown-heading users are the people who set `auto`. Known edge: `auto` together with `commit.status=false` (git then writes no comment block) and a message whose last line starts with a candidate character. I'd add a one-line code comment on it. Cutting `auto` leaves those users with the finding 1 behavior.

## Tests, written first and checked to fail before the fix

**Integration tests** in `checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go`, driving the real hook binary and git's own cleanup (`git -c core.commentChar=X stripspace -s`):
- An editor commit with `;`, `//` (`commentString`) and `auto` gets a final-block trailer with no helper text, and post-commit condenses into it. The `;` case already fails today.
- Amend with `;` and `auto` leaves the message unchanged. The `;` case already fails today.

**Resolver unit tests**, covering the failure modes:
- unset gives `#`;
- `;`;
- `//`;
- both keys set, last one wins;
- `auto` inferred from the comment block;
- `auto` inferred from the scissors line;
- `auto` with no comment block gives `#`;
- a read error gives `#`.

**Trailers unit tests:**
- a no-space and a tab separator are accepted;
- an indented line is still rejected;
- a writer roundtrip case with a no-space final paragraph;
- prose containing the marker is kept, in both orderings;
- `#` and `;` scissors lines cut;
- a CRLF scissors line cuts.

**Attach test:** a commit whose final block says `Entire-Checkpoint:<id>` joins that checkpoint, as on main. This fails today.

I'll also update the existing callers of `addCheckpointTrailerWithComment` and `stampedTrailer` for the new parameter.

## Verification plan

- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`, `mise run test`, `mise run test:integration`, `mise run test:e2e:canary`.
- A real `git commit` and amend in a scratch repo with `;` and `auto`, using the built binary.
- Prepare-commit-msg timing before and after.
- Then one commit, with `progress.md` and `review.md` left untracked. Pushing, the PR description update and the replies each need your separate approval.

## Out of scope (I'll list these in the PR as follow-ups)

- `hasUserContent` and `CommitMsg` still assume `#`.
- Main's `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` also uses substring scissors matching. That one is harmless for deletion.
- The `-m … -e` gap already in the PR body.
- The PR body currently says comment-character support "belongs in a separate change". I'll draft the corrected text for your approval after the fix.

## Copilot reply drafts (to post after the fix is pushed, `<sha>` filled in)

**On [trailers.go:179](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2253#discussion_r4313606824) (scissors):**

> agreed. git only cuts at a line that is exactly `<comment char> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------`, so a prose line containing the marker stays in the commit. i reproduced both orderings: a body trailer above such a line looks final after stripping, and a real final trailer below it disappears. fixed in `<sha>`: `StripEditorComments` now cuts only at the exact scissors line for the configured comment character. added tests for both orderings and a CRLF line.

**On [trailers.go:385](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2253#discussion_r4313606970) (separator):**

> agreed. `git interpret-trailers --parse` reads `Entire-Checkpoint:<id>` and a tab separator as trailers, and main's `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` tests already treat both as trailer lines. fixed in `<sha>`: `trailerLineRe` is now `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:`, shared by the reader and the writer so they still agree. leading whitespace is still rejected. added reader cases and an attach test that joins a no-space trailer.

If you pick the reader-only option, I'll change the second sentence of that reply to match.

Prepare reads the message as git will record it: an editor message loses the
lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the scissors line
down, while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps every line as content. The prefix is
`core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases; the last one set wins),
`#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from the comment block git wrote
into the message; prepare writes its own explanation with the same prefix so
git's cleanup removes it.

I committed the three fixes locally as `866efab31`, on top of the PR head. The branch is 1 commit ahead of origin and merges cleanly with current main (`f36367e6f`). Nothing has been pushed or posted.

## What changed

- **Comment character:** prepare-commit-msg now uses git's real comment prefix: `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (the last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it reads back the character git used in its own comment block. It's used when finding the commit's trailer, when writing Entire's explanation lines, and when placing inherited trailers. `-m`/`-F` commits skip the lookup.
- **Scissors line:** an editor message is cut only at git's exact scissors line, so a prose line that mentions the marker is kept.
- **Separators:** trailer lines accept `Key:value` and a tab after the colon, as git does. The reader and the writer still share one grammar.
- **Docs:** I updated the paragraph in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`.

## Verification

- **Tests failed first, for the expected reasons.**
  - 5 new integration tests running the real hook binary: editor commit and amend with `;` and with `auto`, plus the prose scissors case.
  - The attach no-space test.
  - 7 separator subtests.
  - The new-API unit tests couldn't compile before the change. So after the fix I put the old behaviors back one at a time in scratch copies (repo untouched), and each of the 6 was caught.
- **Real `git commit`**, with git writing the message and doing its own cleanup: all 6 cases pass (default, `;`, `//`, `auto` with a `#` template, amend with `;`, amend with `auto`).
- **Lint:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint` gives 0 issues.
- **Full suite** (`go test -tags=integration -race ./...`): 89 packages ok, including every trailer-authority and adversarial integration test. The failures are all outside this change:
  - hook-chain install, external-agent discovery and external-command signal tests timed out under race-mode load; all pass in isolation;
  - two Antigravity e2e tests fail on the unchanged head too, because they pick up your 1Password commit signing.
- **Canary:** Vogon 53/53, Roger-Roger 4/4.
- **Cost:** about 5.4 ms (median) for one `git config` call, only on editor-source commits. That's about the same as one `git rev-parse`.

**Follow-up, not in this commit:** the commit-msg hook's empty-message check still assumes `#`. Reading the code (I haven't run it): with `;`, quitting the editor without typing still produces a commit instead of aborting. Before this commit that commit held Entire's `#` helper text; now it holds just the trailer. It's about 5 lines plus a test, and could go in before pushing.

## Drafts for your approval

**Reply on [the scissors thread](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2253#discussion_r4313606824):**

> agreed. git only cuts at a line that is exactly `<comment char> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------`, so a prose line containing the marker stays in the commit. i reproduced both orderings: a body trailer above such a line looks final after stripping, and a real final trailer below it disappears. fixed in 866efab31: `StripEditorComments` now cuts only at the exact scissors line for the configured comment character. added tests for both orderings and a CRLF line.

**Reply on [the separator thread](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2253#discussion_r4313606970):**

> agreed. `git interpret-trailers --parse` reads `Entire-Checkpoint:<id>` and a tab separator as trailers, and main's `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` tests already treat both as trailer lines. fixed in 866efab31: `trailerLineRe` is now `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:`, shared by the reader and the writer so they still agree. leading whitespace is still rejected. added reader cases and an attach test that joins a no-space trailer.

**PR description edits:**

1. In **Fix**, replace the paragraph starting "Prepare reads the message as git will record it" with:
   > Prepare reads the message as git will record it (`trailers.StripEditorComments`): an editor message loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down, while a `-m`/`-F` message keeps every line as content. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from the comment block git wrote. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, and never reads the subject paragraph as trailers. The writer from #2259 uses the same `isTrailerBlock` grammar, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.
